I have never understood people who buy upper-tier cars and cheap out on the trim/wheels. No offense to OP, but I personally will always save a bit extra money for a more refined package.

Edit: College student here, so I have no weight in this conversation 🤓 This was mainly aimed towards ICE manufacturers that can’t seem to get stock wheels right.
True, I think these new wheels look amazing on the car.

I should have drawn out my previous comment a bit further, I was mostly referring to manufacturers other than Tesla. Point being because I quite like the line up of rims on all Tesla models. 

In the case of electric cars, sticking with the aero wheels makes 100% sense.
You need to give us some details on what degree(s) you want to pursue.

Accounting definitely sucks for everyone, trust me, you can do it though! I am a STEM major and still managed to get through both Accounting classes (Principles and Managerial), so I know you can do it too!
Not 100% sure how Canadian universities work, but are you asking is it worth to earn the Associates degree and take a few extra courses?
I would definitely go for the actual degree since a certificate won’t really hold up as a foundation of knowledge. Certificates are supposed to be supplementary knowledge based off your degree.
Sounds like your mind is skewed towards to worse. If you think you will be more successful without a degree, try it, see how fortunate you are to attend higher education.
Computer Science and Information Systems start around that and are super in demand.

Computer Science has the most coding out of any technology major lol. It’s primarily going to be math and coding. 

However, coding is such a useful skill to possess, not just for a CompSci job, but for how advance the future will be with technology.

I wonder if you are transferring to my university, we have a College of Informatics specifically for technology majors. 

To answer your question, yes, Informatics is Information Systems plus a bit more! I study Business Informatics which is a combination of Business, Management, and IT/IS.
Suit 100%, do not skimp out on anything.
Contact, the intro song for that album is so amazing!
Perfectly said, no reason to major in Journalism if the school has Communications.
Depends on the field. If your field is STEM, Health, or Business, it is definitely worth it.
If you are going to minor in something, at least choose MIS/IS/BIS—however your school names it. You will be so much more marketable with some technology experience.

You just have to make sure the internship would actually even consider students with a GPA under 3.0. For you and I in the IT field, a minimum 3.0 is required for pretty much everything (from my experience).

Lmao, I co-op in my college and attend classes everyday of the week—10:00 AM - 5:00 PM is my typical day. 

You will be fine with that schedule.
Dang, this is exactly the spec I want! Nice job.
Black trim and wheels, so good looking. Wish these would come to the Model 3!
Haha, I am assuming through aftermarket work?

Not exactly true, if you play your cards correctly with an IS/MIS/BIS degree, you have the potential to become the one who manages CS developers at Google Headquarters. Heck, maybe even a CTO or CIO because you have so much technical knowledge gathered from all departments of the company. 

I would argue there is much more advancement potential for IS/MIS/BIS workers because they can move into lead, manager, director, and officer roles. 

Source: I study Business Informatics, so I have knowledge in IT, management, and business.
I think OP used a 𝘄𝗲𝗯 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹 for that, check this site out: [Beautiful Dingbats](https://beautifuldingbats.com/hey-howd-you-do-that/)
That’s amazing, your dad rocks!

I have been using wired Apple earphones everyday for a few years and it is definitely getting annoying. Especially because the wiring inside is getting a little screwy. Will definitely upgrade to AirPods 2 during the summer.
100% correct, fall time is game time—I locked down my internship back in October.

I wish universities would push students to apply more in the fall. We host our campus-wide career fair in the spring and it’s honestly worthless because most top-tier internship positions are already filled and top-tier companies don’t even bother showing up.

I would advocate to switch into Communications. Not a Comm student, but it’s housed within my college building and seems to be a great program. We also put a emphasis on technology because it’s considered a STEM degree, meaning Comm students are well prepared for whichever discipline they choose (journalism, media, public relations, health, etc.).
